sentences.text:
[The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode] CRL.M.A. 27953/2023 (for exemption)
1. Exemption is allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

This is a petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 Cr.P.C.,
1973 seeking quashing of FIR No. 766/2021 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, 1860 registered with PS- Laxmi Nagar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom on the grounds of settlement.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the parties have resolved their disputes and reduced the terms of the settlement into This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: According to the terms of the settlement, the petitioner No.1 is to pay to respondent No.2 a sum of Rs. 3,30,000/-.
6. Learned counsel further submits that the said amount has already been paid to the respondent No.2 in the interregnum, the receipt whereof is placed at page No. 109 of the present petition.

7. Learned counsel also submits that the parties have already dissolved their marriage under the Muslim Law, by way of Mubarat and the three divorce deeds have also been placed on record as Annexures P3, P4 and P5.
8.
The I.O. is present in person and identifies the parties appearing before the Court today except petitioner No.5.
The I.O. has identified the petitioner No.5 through video call today.
9. This Court has interacted with respondent No.2, who submits that she is aware of the terms of the settlement.

She also affirms the receipt of Rs. 3,30,000/- as full and final settlement for all her claims, as stipulated in the Settlement Agreement and that she has no further claims of whatsoever nature against the petitioner.
She further submits that she has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.
10. This Court has perused the terms of settlement agreement and they appear to be lawful.
The parties are bound by the terms of the settlement.

11. After observing that the disputes are arising from matrimonial ties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the FIR in question and the further criminal This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/10/2023 at 20:53:07 proceedings and it would be in the interest of justice as also of the parties and the society that quietus is put to such disputes.
12.
Accordingly, FIR No. 766/2021 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, 1860 registered with PS-Laxmi Nagar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby quashed.
13. The petition is disposed of accordingly.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J OCTOBER 13, 2023/nd, This is a digitally signed order.
